# tanghoong design system

> The shared visual language for tanghoong.com and every sub-domain. This file
> is the complete specification. An agent that reads it does not need to crawl
> the HTML pages — those exist for humans to look at.
>
> Version: 1.3.1 · Updated: 2026-09-06
> Source of truth: the files in /assets/css/ at https://design.tanghoong.com
> Starter template for a new sub-domain: /template/index.html
> Human documentation: /pages/*.html · Machine documentation: this file
>
> If you are building a page for any *.tanghoong.com property, read this file
> in full first. Do not infer the system from a rendered page — the values here
> are the ones that ship.
>
> Link this file; do not copy it. A token value or a contrast figure pasted
> into another repo's own document goes stale silently — it keeps being read as
> authoritative long after it stopped being true. Your repo may keep its own
> decisions; it may not keep a copy of this spec. scripts/drift.mjs exists
> because five repos did exactly that.

## Read this first

- STARTING A NEW SUB-DOMAIN? Copy /template/index.html. It has the header,
  footer, nav sheet, theme toggle and meta block already wired correctly —
  the details that go wrong when rebuilt by hand are the invisible ones.
- Copy `/assets/css/` into the project. Link in this order: tokens, base,
  layout, components, forms, overlays, content, utilities. Never ship docs.css.
- The stylesheets are the artefact. There is no build step, no framework, no
  webfont, no CSS-in-JS. Plain HTML plus a class.
- Full detail per topic: /pages/brand.html, /pages/foundations.html, /pages/layout.html,
  /pages/components.html, /pages/forms.html, /pages/overlays.html,
  /pages/loading.html, /pages/content.html, /pages/svg.html,
  /pages/patterns.html, /pages/prompt.html

## Non-negotiables

1. Never write a literal colour, font size, radius, shadow or duration in a
   component. Every value comes from a custom property in tokens.css. If the
   value you need does not exist, add it to tokens.css — do not inline it.
2. Never remove a focus outline without replacing it. Focus is `:focus-visible`,
   2px `var(--focus)`, 2px offset.
3. Every interactive control clears a 44px touch target.
4. Every form field has a real `<label for>`. A placeholder is not a label.
5. Colour never carries meaning alone. Pair every status colour with a word.
6. Native element first: `<dialog>` for modals and drawers, `<details>` for
   menus and accordions, real `<button>` and `<a>`.
7. Exactly one `.btn--filled` per view.

## Brand mark

One mark for every property. Geometry, not text — an arc and a circle, so it
never depends on a font being installed. viewBox 0 0 64 64:

  <rect width="64" height="64" rx="14.3" fill="#1d1d1f"/>
  <path d="M37 22a13 13 0 1 0 0 20" fill="none" stroke="#4dff9b"
        stroke-width="5.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  <circle cx="49" cy="32" r="4.6" fill="#4dff9b"/>

It is a "C" and a "·" (the separator this writing already uses). Deliberately
NOT theme-aware, and the ONE place a literal hex is correct: the mark is
embedded in manifests and <img> tags that cannot see the page custom
properties, so it must carry its colours. #4dff9b on #1d1d1f is 12.9:1; the
light accent #03744e on the same tile is 2.89:1, and the green on white is
1.30:1 — which is why the opaque tile exists at all. Minimum size 16px.
Never recolour, never drop the tile, never rebuild the letterform from a font.

Icon set. The <link> order matters — the .ico goes FIRST, or Googlebot guesses
/favicon.ico, 404s, and the search result renders with a blank tile:
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any">
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
  <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
  <link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest">
Files: favicon.svg (master) · favicon.ico (16/32/48) · apple-touch-icon.png
(180) · icon-192.png · icon-512.png. Regenerate rasters from the SVG with
ImageMagick; never hand-edit a generated file.

Header lockup: .brand > svg.brand__mark (28px, aria-hidden, focusable="false")
+ a wordmark span. The link accessible name comes from the wordmark — if it is
visually hidden, keep it in the DOM with .vh.

## Tokens

Declared once with `light-dark(light, dark)`. An explicit theme sets
`data-theme="light"|"dark"` on `<html>`; no attribute follows the OS. Never
define a colour only inside a media query.

Surfaces
  --bg          #fbfbfd / #000000   page ground
  --bg-sunken   #f5f5f7 / #0a0a0c   section bands, wells, chips
  --bg-elevated #ffffff / #1c1c1e   cards, menus, modals
  --bg-glass    72% + blur          sticky header only
Ink
  --text        #1d1d1f / #f5f5f7   body and headings
  --text-2      #515154 / #a1a1a6   supporting copy
  --text-3      #6e6e73 / #86868b   labels, metadata
  --text-hi     #000000 / #ffffff   display only — a hero word, a headline
                                    figure. Not a fourth content level.
Lines (alpha, so they sit on any surface)
  --hairline      #0000001a / #ffffff21   separators, input borders
  --hairline-soft #0000000f / #ffffff14   card and panel outlines
Accent
  --accent      #03744e / #4dff9b
  --accent-ink  #ffffff / #04140b   text on a filled accent
  --accent-wash accent at 12%       tinted buttons, active rows
  --accent-2    #8a5a00 / #ffd38a   optional second voice (kickers, inline
                --accent-2-ink/-wash  marks). Leave unused if not needed.
Status (each has a matching -wash)
  --ok #03744e/#4dff9b · --warn #8a5a00/#f5c451
  --danger #b3261e/#ff6b62 · --info #0a5ec2/#6bb6ff
Chart ramp (six steps out from the accent; --c-1 IS the accent)
  --c-1 #03744e/#4dff9b · --c-2 #268a64/#41e488 · --c-3 #3da07b/#35ca75
  --c-4 #53b792/#29b063 · --c-5 #69ceaa/#1d9751 · --c-6 #7ee6c3/#107f40
  Regenerate at any sample count: node scripts/ramp.mjs <n> [--json]
  --chart-fill 0.16 (area/radar fill) · --chart-grid = --hairline-soft
  Six categories is the ceiling. Group the tail as "Other" or use a table.
Type
  --font-sans  system stack, no webfont
  --font-mono  ui-monospace / SF Mono / Cascadia / JetBrains Mono
  --fs-h1 clamp(2rem, 1.45rem + 2.6vw, 3.25rem)    w660 lh1.08 ls-0.026em
  --fs-h2 clamp(1.5rem, 1.25rem + 1.2vw, 2.25rem)  w620 lh1.15 ls-0.021em
  --fs-h3 clamp(1.25rem, 1.15rem + .5vw, 1.5rem)   w600 lh1.3  ls-0.014em
  --fs-lead / --fs-stat (fluid) · --fs-body 17px · --fs-sm 15px · --fs-xs 13px
  --fs-read clamp(1.3125rem, 1.15rem + .8vw, 1.625rem)  editorial lead only
  Body: lh 1.6, ls -0.006em. Tracking tightens as size grows.
Space (4px scale)
  --s-1 4 · --s-2 8 · --s-3 12 · --s-4 16 · --s-5 20 · --s-6 24 · --s-8 32
  --s-10 40 · --s-12 48 · --s-16 64 · --s-20 80 · --s-24 96 · --s-32 128
Measure
  --container 1120 · --container-prose 720 · --container-mid 940
  --container-wide 1320 · --gutter clamp(20px,5vw,40px)
  --section-y clamp(72px,9vw,128px) · --nav-h 56px
Radius
  --r-sm 10 · --r-md 16 · --r-lg 20 · --r-xl 28 · --r-chip pill (980px)
  Radius steps with box size. A big radius on a small element reads as a bubble.
Shadow
  --sh-sm --sh-md --sh-lg. All resolve to `none` in dark theme: on black a drop
  shadow reads as grime, so depth comes from --bg-elevated instead.
Motion
  --dur-fast .15s (hover, colour) · --dur .26s (transforms, popovers)
  --dur-slow .42s (sheets) · --ease cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)
  --ease-in cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1) for things leaving
Layers
  --z-head 40 · --z-sheet 50 · --z-toast 70 · --z-skip 100
  No --z-modal: a <dialog> opened with showModal() is in the top layer.

## Property skins

A property may re-skin by redefining tokens in its own file, loaded AFTER
tokens.css. tanghoong.com does exactly this — same token set, then a deep
petrol ground (#071a24), sage accent (#b8d9c9), gold second voice (#ffd38a),
forced dark. Every component still works because none of them names a colour.

MAY redefine: the four surfaces · the four inks · both hairlines · --accent and
  its ink/wash · --accent-2 · --fs-read · container widths · color-scheme.
MUST NOT touch: the space scale · the radius scale · --ease and durations ·
  the status colours · the focus treatment · the mark.
Rules: re-run scripts/contrast.mjs against the skinned values, and on a
coloured ground tint the hairlines to match (#dcf1f52e, not plain white alpha —
neutral alpha over petrol reads as grey scum).
Never edit tokens.css in a consuming repo. That is a fork, not a skin.

## Editorial type

For a landing page where a short paragraph carries the weight:
  .read       --fs-read, line-height 1.48, ls -0.027em, max-width 30rem
  .read-body  --fs-sm, line-height 1.8, --text-2, max-width 30rem
  .meta-mono  mono, --fs-xs, POSITIVE tracking 0.08em, uppercase, --text-3
The measure comes DOWN as the size goes up — 30rem, not 68ch. Mono uppercase
metadata is the counterweight to large warm type: tiny, technical, precise.

## Layout

A page is a stack of `<section class="section s-page|s-sunken">`, alternating
surfaces to band the scroll. Inside each, one `.container`.

  .container [--prose|--mid|--wide|--flush]
  .section [--tight|--flush] · .s-page / .s-sunken
  .sec-head > div > h2 + p.sec-head__intro   (title left, action right)
  .grid [--2|--3|--4] [--gap-lg]             mobile-first, minmax(0,1fr) tracks
  .with-aside [--start] + aside.rail         two-column reading layout
  .cluster (wrapping row, gap --s-3) · .stack [--lg] (owl selector)
  .site-head > .container.head-in > .brand + nav.head-nav + .head-end
    .head-end holds exactly two icon buttons: theme toggle, then
    .navsheet__trigger. No CTA in the corner — it competes with the hero one.
    900px: .head-nav appears, .navsheet__trigger hides. Theme is always shown.
    The theme button carries THREE icons — .ic.ic--auto, .ic.ic--light,
    .ic.ic--dark — and CSS shows one based on the data-theme attribute. Do not
    swap the icon from script: driving it off the attribute is what stops the
    icon drifting out of sync with the theme it claims to show.
  .site-foot > .container > .foot-grid + .foot-legal

Rhythm rule: the section owns vertical padding, the grid owns gaps.
Components carry NO outer margin. Never put margin-bottom on a component.

Breakpoints, range syntax only. They are content breakpoints, not devices:
  640  footer to 3 col · .facts to 2 col · form grids split
  720  cards and grids to 2 col · .row puts meta right
  900  header nav/tools/CTA appear, mobile sheet trigger hides
  960  grids to 3–4 col · aside rail becomes sticky

## Components

Buttons  .btn + --filled|--tinted|--quiet|--outline|--danger
         sizes --sm|--lg|--icon|--block · .iconbtn (bordered icon button)
         .link-more (inline link with a nudging arrow)
Labels   .chip [--outline|--accent] passive: a topic or tag, no state
         .badge [--ok|--warn|--danger|--info|--solid] + .badge__dot, carries state
Surfaces .card (+__title __desc __status __foot __arrow) inside .cards [--2|--3]
           lifts on hover only when it is an <a>. __foot uses margin-top:auto.
         .panel [--elevated|--flat] (+__head __title __foot) sunken well, no hover
         .band centred CTA · .note [--ok|--warn|--danger|--info] + __title
Data     .stats [--4] > .stat__fig .stat__label .stat__note (tabular-nums)
         .rows > li > .row (+__title __desc __meta) — use past ~6 items
         .facts (dl, uppercase dt) · .empty (+__title) · .meter > .meter__fill
         .table inside .table-wrap — the WRAPPER scrolls, never the page body
         .table--compact · td.num for right-aligned tabular figures
Nav      .crumb · .tabs · .divider · .avatar [--sm|--lg]

## Forms

  .field > .label + .input|.textarea|.select + .hint|.error
  .input-group > .input-group__addon + .input   (border lives on the group)
  .check > input + .check__body > .check__label + .check__hint
  .check--boxed  selectable card, uses :has(input:checked)
  .switch > input + .switch__track + label text
  .fieldset > .fieldset__legend + .fieldset__intro
  .form-grid [--2] with .span-2 · .form-actions
  sizes .input--sm|--lg · .textarea--code · .range · .file

Errors use `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby`, NOT a class — the
attribute a screen reader uses is the one that turns the field red.
Validate on blur and on submit, never on keystroke.
Mark optional fields, not required ones.
A switch applies immediately; a checkbox applies on submit.

## Overlays

  .modal   <dialog>, .showModal(). Centred; becomes a bottom sheet under 480px.
  .drawer [--start]  <dialog>, full height, pinned to an edge.
  .navsheet  the mobile menu — a .drawer, opened by .navsheet__trigger
  .menu    <details> + .menu__list [--end] + .menu__sep
  .accordion > .accordion__item (<details>) + .accordion__chev
  .toasts (top-centre, aria-live) > .toast [--warn|--danger] + .toast__icon
  .tip > .tip__bubble [.tip--start|--end|--below for edges]

Two traps, both already handled in the CSS — do not reintroduce them:
1. base.css resets `* { margin: 0 }`, which kills the UA `dialog { margin:auto }`
   and pins a dialog to the corner. .modal and .drawer restore margin explicitly.
2. `backdrop-filter` on .site-head makes it a containing block for
   position:fixed descendants. The nav sheet MUST be a sibling of <header>,
   never a child, or it gets trapped in the header box.

## Loading and async state

Pick by what you know, not by habit:
  under ~300ms   show NOTHING — a spinner that flashes reads as a glitch
  shape known    .skel (+ --text --title --chip --avatar --btn --media)
  shape unknown  .spinner (+ --sm --lg) — submits, searches, saves
  route change   .progress--top, a 2px bar under the header
  real percent   .meter, always. A number beats a moving stripe.
  refresh in place  .async[aria-busy] dims .async__content — do NOT swap in a
                    skeleton, it loses the reader's place

A skeleton exists to stop the layout jumping — that is its whole job. Build it
from the SAME component as the real thing (.card etc) so padding, gap and
radius match and the two boxes are the same height. Sizes are in em. The last
text line is 72% wide; real paragraphs do not end flush. Sweep, never pulse —
a pulse reads as broken. Do not skeleton a list of unknown length; show 3-4.

Every fetching region has FOUR states — loading, loaded, empty, error. A page
that designs only the happy one ships the other three by accident. Empty is not
an error (give them the action); an error is not empty (say what failed, offer
a retry).

Announcing: aria-busy="true" on the waiting region · role="status" on a short
progress message · role="alert" on the error that replaces it · aria-label on a
skeleton container. 🔴 NEVER leave aria-busy set after the request finishes —
the region is then permanently "updating" to a screen reader while looking
normal to everyone else. Clear it where you remove the spinner.

## Motion boundaries

Motion is feedback and continuity. It confirms something happened, or carries
the eye between states. It is never ornament, and nothing moves on its own.

SANCTIONED — this is the complete list:
  colour/background change  --dur-fast   hover and focus on any control
  scale to 0.97             --dur-fast   :active on buttons
  lift 2px + shadow         --dur        hover on a card that is a link
  arrow nudge 3px           --dur        .link-more, .card__arrow
  fade + 4px rise           --dur-fast   menus and popovers
  fade + scale 0.97         --dur        modal entrance
  slide from edge           --dur-slow   drawers and the nav sheet
  chevron rotate 180°       --dur        accordion open
  skeleton sweep            1.4s loop    placeholders only
  spinner rotate            0.7s loop    indeterminate waits only

NOT IN THIS SYSTEM:
  scroll-triggered reveals (breaks find-in-page, print and fast readers)
  parallax, tilt, magnetic cursors, spring/bounce/elastic easing
  autoplaying decoration: pulsing dots, breathing gradients, animated mesh
    (the ONLY permitted infinite animations are the skeleton and the spinner,
     and both mean "waiting")
  page transitions that delay navigation
  animating height/width/top/margin — only opacity and transform stay on the
    compositor; the rest force layout every frame

The test: if the animation were removed, would anything be harder to
understand? If not, it is ornament — cut it.

JS-driven motion must read the preference itself:
matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches — base.css cannot
reach it, and neither can it reach animation inside a standalone .svg file.

## Titles and meta

  <title>       "Page name — Site name", em dash with spaces. ≤60 chars.
                Page name FIRST: a tab truncates from the right, and at eight
                visible characters the page name is the only distinguishing part.
                A sub-domain home page drops the repetition — "tanghoong design
                system", not "Home — tanghoong design system".
  description   ≤160 chars, one sentence, written for a person.
  og:title      same as <title>. og:image 1200x630, required or links preview blank.
  h1            one per page; may be shorter than the title, which carries the
                site name where the h1 does not.
Keep the site name byte-identical across a property.

## Prose

`.prose` on the wrapper, then unclassed HTML inside — Markdown output drops
straight in. Spacing is the owl selector `.prose > * + *`. Caps at 68ch.
  .lede 56ch · .quote / blockquote 60ch + .quote-note
  .eyebrow (uppercase label above a heading) · .article-head + .article-meta
  .steps (CSS counter, mono accent numbers) · .codeblock · .code-inline · .kbd
  .measure 68ch · .measure-tight 56ch · .measure-wide 80ch
  .measure-headline 20ch · --tight 16ch  (big type needs a much tighter cap)
Links inside .prose underline always; hover-only is undiscoverable mid-paragraph.
content.css ends with a print block that drops all chrome.

## SVG and data graphics

Icons: 24px viewBox, rendered 16-20px, `fill="none" stroke="currentColor"`,
`stroke-linecap/linejoin="round"`. Stroke width tracks RENDERED size, not the
viewBox: 12-14px→2.4, 16px→2, 18-20px→1.8, 24px+→1.5. Never hard-code a hex in
an icon — currentColor is what makes it work on a filled button and in both
themes. Decorative → `aria-hidden="true"` with the label on the control.
Meaningful → `role="img"` + an aria-label stating the actual figures.

### The card system

Self-contained SVG cards (the github.com/tanghoong profile README pattern —
generated by scripts/generate-cards.mjs, committed as static files, no
third-party badge service in the render path):
  880px wide always, so a column of cards aligns. Height varies: 168 stat row,
  208 stats/two-panel, 268 columns, 276 share bar, 336 radar, 356 blocks,
  428 year clock. Order the column most-signal-first; tallest and most
  decorative last, where its height costs the reader nothing.
  frame: <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" rx="20" fill=--bg-elevated
         stroke #000 @0.1 light / #fff @0.13 dark>   (rx 20 = --r-lg)
  the 0.5 offset keeps a 1px stroke crisp — a whole-pixel edge renders as 2px
  padding 24 · title baseline y=36 · subtitle y=54 · plot area starts y=84
  (y=40 for the title when there is no subtitle; left margin 54 when the plot
  needs axis values; two-panel cards split at 24..416 and 464..856)

### Type in SVG (raw px — SVG has no rem, so it ignores the user font setting)

  30/700/-0.9   headline figure in a stat column
  20/700/-0.6   secondary figure
  14/600/-0.2   card title
  12/600/-0.07  panel heading, series name
  11/600/-0.07  label inside a filled block
  10/600/+0.7   UPPERCASE stat label — positive tracking, it is set in caps
  10/400/-0.06  card subtitle, date range, footnote
  9/600/-0.05   axis caption   ·  9/400/-0.06  axis value
  8.5/600/-0.05 month label on the year clock — the floor
Same stack as --font-sans. Every figure gets font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums.
Nothing essential may live only in SVG text; it must also be in the aria-label.

### The ramp is a function, not a palette

Interpolate --c-from → --c-to and sample at N, IN OKLAB not sRGB. sRGB looks
like the obvious choice and produces perceptually uneven steps that bunch at
one end — the first version of this ramp did that and three of its six steps
were indistinguishable. Use scripts/ramp.mjs. Light #03744e → #7ee6c3;
dark #4dff9b → #107f40. Index 0 is the largest series and IS the accent. The overview card
samples 6, frameworks 10, languages 16 — all from the same two endpoints.
--c-1..--c-6 are the six-sample case, for CSS which cannot interpolate.
Six is the ceiling *for a legend*; past that, label each block in place or
use a table. As the ramp lightens, label ink must flip from white to dark —
roughly at the fourth step. That is the thing careless automation gets wrong.

### Charting idioms

  stat row      3 columns centred at 880/6, 880/2, 880*5/6; dividers at the
                thirds; figure + UPPERCASE label + a line giving it a denominator
  share bar     one rounded track (rx = height/2, 8-10px tall), segments as
                plain paths over it — no clipPath needed, the track corners show
  blocks        width proportional, height constant, rx=10, 4px gutter, labels
                inset 9px IN PLACE — this is how a card carries 10+ series
  columns       gridlines behind the data in --chart-grid, axis values in the
                left margin, columns scaleY from the baseline
  radar         6 axes, 3 rings, accent polygon at fill-opacity 0.16 (not the
                12% --accent-wash: this sits over gridlines and needs more body)
  year clock    polar, inner r52 outer r124 — the hole matters, spokes
                converging on a point smear. Length AND colour carry the count,
                so it survives greyscale. For the shape of a year, not for
                reading a value off.
  comparison    one pill per period; solid fill = now, dashed accent @0.45 with
                stroke-dasharray="3 3" = the reference being measured against

### Motion

Five animations, all cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) = --ease:
  .fade 260ms  opacity 0 + translateY(6px)   type, labels, gridlines (most used)
  .rise 420ms  opacity 0 + translateY(12px)  headline figures, whole blocks
  .grow 420ms  scaleX(0)                     horizontal bars, share segments
  .bar  420ms  scaleY(0)                     vertical columns from the baseline
  .draw 900ms  stroke-dashoffset             a trend line drawing on; ≤1 per card
260ms is --dur, 420ms is --dur-slow. Stagger 0.04-0.06s within a group, ~0.12s
between groups; past ~0.6s total the reader is waiting, not watching.

### Two SVG-specific traps

1. An SVG carries its own <style>, so base.css's global reduced-motion rule
   cannot reach inside it. Repeat the guard as
   `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { … }` in every animated SVG.
2. An <img src="*.svg"> cannot see the page custom properties. Inline SVG uses
   var(--token) and currentColor; a file-loaded SVG needs a light/dark pair
   switched with <picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">.
   The <img alt> must carry the real figures, not "stats card".
Also: transform-origin must be set explicitly in user units on anything that
scales or rotates — an SVG element's default origin is the viewport corner, so
without it every bar grows from the top-left of the whole card.

## Utilities

.t2 .t3 .t-accent .t-danger · .sm .xs .lead · .mono .nums · .w-med .w-semi
.center .end .mx-auto · .measure* · .vh (visually hidden, still announced)
.hidden .flex-1 .no-wrap .truncate .clamp-2 .clamp-3 · .scroll-x
.mt-2 .mt-3 .mt-4 .mt-6 .mt-8 .mt-12 .mt-16  (top margin only — bottom margins
fight the owl selector)
Every [id] gets scroll-margin-block-start so anchors clear the sticky header.

## Writing markup

- Build from the vocabulary above before writing any new CSS. A genuinely new
  component goes in the right layer file with a comment saying what it is for
  and when NOT to use it.
- Prefer logical properties: inline-size/block-size, inset-*, margin-inline,
  border-inline-start. The system ships in English and Chinese.
- SVG icons 16–20px, `fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8–2"`,
  always `aria-hidden="true"`. An icon-only control needs `aria-label`.
- One `<h1>` per page. Never skip a heading level. To render text at heading
  size without being a heading, style a `<p>` — do not add a second `<h1>`.

## Avoid

- A second primary button in the same view.
- A shadow in dark theme (they are `none`; use --bg-elevated for depth).
- A tooltip carrying information available nowhere else.
- A fifth breakpoint — try clamp(), minmax() or auto-fill first.
- `vh` for full-height overlays; use `dvh` or mobile browser chrome clips them.
- Any animation that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## Checking a page you generated

  node scripts/conform.mjs <file.html> --fail   structural conformance
  node scripts/contrast.mjs --fail              only if you touched tokens.css
  node scripts/drift.mjs --fail                 run from the design repo, over
                                                the repos that consume it

conform.mjs enforces the rules in this file and reports error/warn/info. A
deliberate exception is declared in the page, not by weakening the rule:
  <!-- conform:allow rule-id — the reason -->
drift.mjs reports values this system has retired, hexes within ΔE 0.02 of a
live token without being it, and contrast figures that do not survive being
recomputed. Same waiver form: <!-- drift:allow — the reason -->
All three are dependency-free Node. None can see computed styles or
runtime behaviour: they are a first pass, not a substitute for opening the page
in both themes and tabbing through it.

## Ship checklist

No literal hex/px/radius/duration outside tokens.css · both themes checked in
both toggle directions · tabbed the whole page, focus ring visible everywhere ·
every field labelled, every error wired with aria-invalid + aria-describedby ·
every icon-only control has aria-label · one .btn--filled per view · no
horizontal scroll at 320px · heading levels unbroken · checked with reduced
motion forced on · print preview clean.
